Article Title: AI giant Anthropic to make Wall Street debut next month; could be biggest ever initial public sale of stock: Key details from Claude maker's filing
Article Text:
Anthropic has proposed a dual-class share structure

Who will lead the IPO, and how will shares be structured

A public-benefit company with an AI safety mission

Revenue growth, legal costs and the wider AI market

Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind Claude, has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in the US, taking a major step towards what could become one of the biggest stock market listings in history.The company said it had submitted a registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a proposed offering of its Class A common stock.Anthropic plans to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The company has not yet determined the number of shares it will offer or the price range for the IPO. The proposed listing, which could take place as early as next month, will test investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies amid growing scrutiny of the sector's spending, profitability and long-term growth prospects.Valued at $965 billion after its May 2026 funding round, Anthropic has emerged as one of the biggest players in the global AI industry.Anthropic has appointed a group of major investment banks to underwrite the proposed offering. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Securities and Citigroup are among the underwriters, alongside RBC Capital Markets, UBS Securities, BMO Capital Markets and BNP Paribas.The filing outlines a share structure that distinguishes between voting and non-voting stock.Each share of Class A common stock will carry one vote, while Class N common stock will have no voting rights. The company said its Class N shareholders are primarily strategic business partners.Anthropic also plans to issue a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company established by its co-founders, known as Founder LLC. The filing further states that the Class A common stock will not be convertible.Chief executive Dario Amodei holds 240.6 million Class A shares before the offering, with the total rising to 245.3 million when shares subject to voting proxies are included.The company has also contributed 846,840,960 shares of Class N common stock to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund LLC, reflecting its public-benefit structure.Anthropic operates as a public benefit corporation, the statement said with a legal structure that requires its management to balance financial performance with broader public interests. The company said it intends to direct a meaningful portion of its resources towards ensuring that frontier AI is safe and that its benefits are widely distributed.The structure sets Anthropic apart from a conventional profit-focused company, particularly as it prepares to answer to public-market investors. Its commitment to AI safety will be closely watched alongside its commercial performance, given wider concerns about the risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems.Anthropic also said it does not expect to pay dividends in the foreseeable future, signalling that it intends to retain resources for its business and future investments.Anthropic's filing comes as investors weigh the company's rapid expansion against the substantial costs and risks associated with developing advanced AI systems.The company recorded a $1.5 billion charge in the three months ended September 30, 2025, to settle the Bartz litigation, a copyright dispute brought by authors who alleged that their books had been used without permission to train Claude. The settlement highlights the legal liabilities that can accompany the development of generative AI models.The IPO is also expected to provide a clearer picture of the economics underpinning the AI boom. Anthropic and rival OpenAI sit at the centre of a network of chipmakers, cloud providers, data-centre operators and other businesses that have invested heavily in anticipation of sustained demand for AI services.
Article Summary: Anthropic plans to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “ANT’ The company has not yet determined the number of shares it will offer or the price range for the IPO. The proposed listing, which could take place as early as next month, will test investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies.

Article Title: E100 cars get regulatory green light ahead of planned launches
Article Text:
Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol-blended petrol

NEW DELHI: Government on Monday notified a change in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, allowing flex-fuel vehicles that can run on upto 100% ethanol blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models.An official said the amendments update the emission provisions by including E100 alongside E85. Officials said E85 and E100 are "intended only for vehicles specially designed and certified to use it and will not be applicable for other vehicles. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel. This notification doesn't require owners of existing vehicles to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles either at present or in future. "Officials said Flex Fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US. These vehicles are specially designed to operate on a range of ethanol and petrol blends using a single tank fuel. Depending on the vehicle's design and certification, this range may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Officials also said that ethanol has lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.
Article Summary: Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol- blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel.

Article Title: Oil price today: Brent crude holds firm at $115 per barrel, WTI trades at $100
Article Text:
Oil prices continue to inch higher

Oil prices edged higher again on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing $115 a barrel after declining in previous sessions. The rebound came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery, reviving concerns over oil supplies from the Middle East amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its proxies.Brent crude gained $1.22, or 1.07%, to trade at $115.10, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $0.96, or 0.96%, to $100.90.The Houthis on Tuesday said that they targeted the refinery, which has a processing capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. The claimed strike marked an escalation in their attacks against Saudi Arabia, the world's second-largest crude producer. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the attack.The latest gains followed a decline of nearly $2 in oil prices on Tuesday, when talks in the Middle East helped ease concerns over supply disruptions. The reported strike brought those concerns back into focus.Expectations of higher crude inventories in the US provided another factor for the oil market to consider. US crude stockpiles increased by around 15,000 barrels in the week ended October 23, according to a Reuters poll of eight analysts.On the production front, OPEC+ members are expected to maintain their December oil output targets at Sunday's meeting, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. The expected decision is in line with market expectations.Output in most of the group's seven core members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, is already below their respective production targets.Meanwhile, Russia's crude oil shipments from its Baltic and Black Sea ports could decrease next month, traders said.The potential decline comes as Russian domestic refiners prepare to increase diesel production following a deal with Washington this month.Oil prices have remained volatile as the Middle East crisis enters its eighth month. However, the latest spike remains below the $126-per-barrel peak recorded earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude gained $1.22, or 1.07%, to trade at $115.10, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $0.96, or 0.96%, to $100.90. The rebound came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, reviving concerns over oil supplies.

Article Title: Rs 25,000 crore in taxes, 12 lakh jobs: Vaishnaw backs mobile PLI scheme
Article Text:
Union minister for railways, information & broadcasting, and electronics & IT Ashwini Vaishnaw

NEW DELHI: India's mobile phone manufacturing sector has generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections, exceeding the Rs 19,000 crore paid out by the government as incentives under its production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme.Union minister for electronics and information technology Ashwini Vaishnaw shared the figures on Wednesday while dismissing news reports that questioned the effectiveness of India's mobile manufacturing model.He added that the scheme had also contributed Rs 3,000 crore in Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections.Highlighting the sector's employment contribution, Vaishnaw said, "Electronics manufacturing employs 25 Lakh people; mobile manufacturing alone employs 12 Lakh."The government is now looking to build on the sector's manufacturing base through a new scheme focused on expanding production, increasing the domestic sourcing of components and strengthening India's position in global supply chains.The Union Cabinet approved the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS) in July, allocating Rs 62,500 crore to the programme. It will operate from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.The scheme is designed to scale up mobile phone production, increase domestic value addition, strengthen supply chains and improve the industry's global competitiveness.Incentives for eligible mobile phone sales range from 2.25% to 5%, with an additional benefit of up to 1.5% for domestic sourcing of key components and sub-assemblies.Support for Indian mobile brands is also part of the programme, with incentives linked to design and research and development.According to the ministry of electronics and information technology, mobile phone production over the scheme's tenure is expected to total approximately Rs 39 lakh crore, with exports also projected to rise significantly. The programme is expected to create around 60,000 direct jobs.The new initiative comes after the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing ended on March 31, 2026. The government's focus is now on sustaining manufacturing growth while promoting deeper domestic sourcing and Indian-owned mobile brands.
Article Summary: India's mobile phone manufacturing sector has generated Rs 25,000 crore in direct tax collections. Union minister for electronics and information technology Ashwini Vaishnaw shared the figures on Wednesday. He added that the scheme had also contributed Rs 3,000 euros in Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections.

Article Title: Mukesh Ambani gets teary-eyed as Anant, Akash, Isha talk about Reliance's journey at Jio listing
Article Text:
Mukesh Ambani gets emotional while listening to Anant and Isha Ambani’s address during Jio Platforms IPO ceremony

Isha Ambani recalls father's early days at Reliance

Isha planted Jio's idea, says brother Anant

Akash Ambani calls listing a ‘start line’

Jio share listing: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani got emotional at Jio Platforms Limited’s listing ceremony as he watched his children speak about the family’s legacy and Jio’s journey. Sitting beside his wife, Nita Ambani, the 69-year-old chairman listened as Isha, Akash and Anant Ambani addressed the gathering ahead of the NSE bell-ringing ceremony.The occasion was particularly significant for Reliance, marking its first listing in two decades with the stock market debut of Jio Platforms Limited. The ceremony brought together the company’s history, the contribution of its founders and the responsibility its next generation now carries.Jio Platforms made a strong debut on Dalal Street, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of 21.36% over its IPO issue price of Rs 1,119 per share. The Rs 30,213-crore public issue was subscribed 22.19 times, making it India's largest IPO to date and valuing the Reliance Industries-backed digital services business at over Rs 10 lakh crore.Isha Ambani, executive director of Reliance Retail Ventures, took the gathering back to the company's beginnings, recalling a recent family dinner during which her father spoke about Reliance's first public offering in 1977.Mukesh Ambani was 20 at the time, while his father, Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take the company to the public."A few evenings ago, at our dinner table, my father, Shri Mukesh Ambani, was remembering his days in 1977. He was 20 years old, working on Reliance's first public offering. My grandfather, Shri Dhirubhai Ambani, had decided to take Reliance to the people," she said.Isha also recalled the maxim associated with her grandfather, 'Growth is life', and vowed to continue building the business and creating value for shareholders. She said Akash had worked hard for 13 years to build and grow Jio into India's largest telecom company, with over 53 crore subscribers.Anant Ambani, executive director of Reliance Industries, recalled how Jio grew from an idea planted by his sister Isha and nurtured by her twin brother, Akash. Reflecting on Reliance’s journey and its global ambitions, he said, “Once-barren land of Jamnagar turned into the site of the world's largest refinery. He showed the world that when India builds, the world takes notice. Then came the New India, the young India, and a new dream: internet in every hand and the world within reach of every village. The name of that dream was Jio. The seed of this dream was planted by Isha Didi, and Akash Bhai made that seed his own dream. Jio was then taken to every corner of the country.”The ceremony also highlighted the scale of investor interest in the company. Akash said that the IPO received demand worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore through 1.3 crore applications, with the issue fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its launch. He described the response as deeply humbling and said it had left him with a profound sense of responsibility.The entire Ambani family, including the next generation, rang the bell as the clock struck 10 am. By 11.01 am, Jio Platforms shares were trading 21.42% higher at Rs 1,358.7 on the BSE, against a 0.89% decline in the benchmark index.Jio Platforms managing director Akash Ambani said the listing was not a finish line but a start line. He promised to take the company to greater heights and grow investor wealth, as Reliance Industries has done over nearly 50 years."We promise to take Jio to greater heights of growth, excellence and reputation in India and the world," the 35-year-old said at the NSE ceremony, attended by his parents, siblings and grandmother Kokilaben.Akash said the next generation's responsibility was not simply to preserve what it had inherited, but to make Jio bigger, better and more meaningful for India.He said Jio had democratised data in its first decade and would now focus on making more technologies accessible."In our next ten (years), we want to democratise every technology that can transform Indian lives: AI, cloud, connected devices, connectivity even from space and digital services not yet imagined," he said.Akash described the company's ambition as building a digital society where connectivity, computing and intelligence work together seamlessly. He said India was emerging as a creator of technology rather than merely a consumer. "We are now ready to take the tricolour global", he added.
Article Summary: Jio Platforms made a strong debut on Dalal Street, listing at Rs 1,359 on the BSE and NSE. The Rs 30,213-crore public issue was subscribed 22.19 times, making it India's largest IPO to date and valuing the Reliance Industries-backed digital services business at over Rs 10 lakh crore.

Article Title: Jio share price: JPL makes strong debut at 21% premium; becomes India's second-most valuable firm - all you need to know
Article Text:
Jio Platforms Limited registers strong stock market debut

Jio Platforms listing: All you need to know

Stellar listing

Reliance Industries: Rs 15.89 lakh crore Jio Platforms: Rs 12.50 lakh crore Bharti Airtel: Rs 12.05 lakh crore HDFC Bank: Rs 10.42 lakh crore ICICI Bank: Rs 9.80 lakh crore

Blockbuster IPO attracted bids worth over Rs 7.4 lakh crore

Grey market premium indicated a strong listing

Jio's future ambitions

Jio stock price: Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with its shares listing at Rs 1,358 on the BSE and NSE, a premium of around 21.35% over the issue price of Rs 1,119. The stock touched a high of Rs 1,375 and a low of Rs 1,356.40 during early trade. The listing comes after a record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) that attracted substantial demand from institutional and retail investors.The debut placed Jio Platforms among India's most valuable listed companies, with a market capitalisation of around Rs 12.5 lakh crore. It became the country's second most valuable company by market valuation, behind parent Reliance Industries . The IPO attracted bids worth more than Rs 7.4 lakh crore across the public issue and anchor investor placement, while applications approached 1.39 crore.Jio Platforms listed on the BSE and NSE at Rs 1,358 per share, around 21.35% above its issue price of Rs 1,119. During early trade, the stock touched a high of Rs 1,375 and a low of Rs 1,356.40.Its market valuation stood at Rs 12,50,586.39 crore during early deals on the BSE, placing it second in India's market capitalisation rankings, behind Reliance Industries.The top five companies by market capitalisation were:The combined market valuation of Jio Platforms and Reliance Industries stood at Rs 28.40 lakh crore.Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO closed with bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer. Total demand across the public issue and anchor investor placement crossed Rs 7.4 lakh crore, while applications approached 1.39 crore.The offering was entirely a fresh issue of 27 crore shares, with the price band set at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. The IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23.Jio Platforms' IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening, making it the fastest-subscribed mega public issue in India. At the listing ceremony, managing director Akash Ambani said the offering had been fully subscribed within 95 minutes of launch.“The response surpassed our imagination, breaking records in every investor category. We were fully subscribed for India's largest IPO within 95 minutes of launch, the fastest ever India has seen,” he said.The IPO's Rs 8,110 crore anchor book attracted institutional demand of more than Rs 2.5 lakh crore, exceeding the amount on offer by over 30 times.Bids from qualified institutional buyers reached 70.55 times the shares reserved for their category, contributing to the issue's overall subscription of 22.19 times.Ahead of the listing, Jio Platforms shares were quoting at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 22%. On Tuesday, October 20, the premium stood at about Rs 245.Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119, this indicated a possible listing price of Rs 1,364, implying a premium of nearly 22%, according to unofficial grey market quotes.GMP refers to the premium speculators in the unofficial market are prepared to pay for shares of a company awaiting its IPO listing.Speaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani said that the response to the IPO had exceeded expectations. He pledged to take the company forward alongside his siblings, Isha and Anant.“We promise to take Jio to greater heights of growth, excellence, and reputation in India and the world,” he said.Ambani described the listing as the beginning of a new phase for the company and emphasised its responsibility towards its new shareholders.“Today's listing, as Isha said, is not a finish line, but a starting line. We will communicate openly, honor our commitments and earn your trust through our actions,” he said.Speaking at the listing ceremony, Akash Ambani said that Jio aims to democratise technology with the potential to transform Indian lives over the next ten years, including through connectivity from space. The company's ambition, he added, is to build a digital society with Jio Platforms at its core, where connectivity, computing and intelligence work together seamlessly.Ambani said the company would continue to focus on expanding digital access and creating value for customers and investors. He also said the next generation of Ambanis had a responsibility to make Jio bigger, better and more meaningful for India, rather than merely preserve what they had inherited.Jio's homegrown platforms now serve more than 540 million customers, Ambani said, adding that the company would seek to build on its digital infrastructure and services.“As trustees of your wealth, our duty is to protect it, grow it decade after decade. The only way is by creating disproportionate value for our customers,” he said.The listing ceremony was attended by Akash Ambani's parents, Mukesh Ambani and Nita Ambani, along with his siblings and grandmother, Kokilaben.
Article Summary: Jio Platforms made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, with its shares listing at Rs 1,358 on the BSE and NSE. The listing comes after a record- breaking initial public offering (IPO) that attracted substantial demand from institutional and retail investors. The IPO attracted bids worth more than Rs 7.4 lakh crore across the public issue and anchor investor placement.

Article Title: Microfinance borrowers can now repay loans anywhere, anytime through NPCI initiative
Article Text:
In a notable collaboration, NPCI Bharat BillPay has joined forces with NABARD Financial Services to expand digital loan repayment avenues for borrowers.

MUMBAI: Through a new partnership, microfinance borrowers can now conveniently repay their loans using any of over 1,000 banking and payment apps or 8 lakh local collection agents via Bharat Connect.NPCI Bharat BillPay (NBBL), a wholly owned subsidiary of NPCI, has onboarded NABARD Financial Services (NABFINS), a subsidiary of NABARD, on the platform under its Loan Repayment category. The integration will cover over 1 lakh NABFINS customers across 19 states and allow them to pay EMIs and overdue instalments through digital and assisted channels.Canara Bank facilitated the onboarding as the Biller Operating Unit (BOU). According to Dr Y Haragopal, managing director of NABFINS, the partnership will make loan repayments more accessible to customers in underserved communities. "Our association with NPCI Bharat Connect is another step towards enabling seamless, secure, and convenient digital payment solutions for our customers. This initiative reinforces our commitment to leverage technology to promote financial inclusion and enhance customer experience," he said.According to Sunil Kumar Chugh, executive director of Canara Bank, the integration will expand digital loan repayment options for microfinance borrowers. "This integration marks an important milestone in enabling seamless and convenient digital loan repayment solutions for borrowers, particularly in the microfinance sector. Canara Bank remains committed to fostering digital innovation and strengthening the digital payment ecosystem, thereby contributing to greater financial inclusion and enhanced customer convenience across the country," he said.According to Dr Noopur Chaturvedi, MD and CEO of NBBL, the integration will extend the platform's interoperable payment network to microfinance borrowers. "Through this integration, we are enabling borrowers to benefit from Bharat Connect's expanding and interoperable network, making loan repayments more accessible, convenient, and seamless," she said.The Loan Repayment category has over 400 billers, including banks, non-banking financial companies and microfinance institutions. In the first half of FY27, it processed over 18.8 crore transactions worth around Rs 1.23 lakh crore, with transaction volume rising 18% year on year and transaction value increasing 31%.NBBL operates Bharat Connect, an interoperable platform for bill payments and collections. Its services include consumer bill payments, business-to-business collections, invoice management, reconciliation and access to structured financing options. Its Banking Connect platform enables interoperability between banks and payment aggregators for merchant transactions. NBBL is also the settlement agency for the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).
Article Summary: NPCI Bharat BillPay has joined forces with NABARD Financial Services to expand digital loan repayment avenues for borrowers. The integration will cover over 1 lakh NABFINS customers across 19 states and allow them to pay EMIs and overdue instalments.

Article Title: Air India partners SBI Card to combine spend reward with loyalty benefits
Article Text:
Air India has teamed up with SBI Card to launch a travel credit card designed to elevate the Maharaja Club loyalty programme.

MUMBAI: Air India has partnered SBI Card to offer a credit card that will combine Maharaja Club loyalty benefits with rewards on everyday spending and travel. The card, being developed with Visa, will offer travel and lifestyle benefits to members of the airline's loyalty programme.According to Nipun Aggarwal, chief commercial officer of Air India, the partnership aims to increase the appeal of Maharaja Club by rewarding customers for everyday spending and travel. "Together with SBI Card and Visa, our goal is to build India's most compelling travel credit card programme and make Maharaja Club the loyalty currency of choice for millions of Indians," he said.According to Salila Pande, MD and CEO of SBI Card, the card will cater to changing travel preferences and spending needs. "Through this strategic partnership, we aim to create a compelling travel-focussed credit card that delivers rewarding experiences to customers," she said.Maharaja Club has added over five million members since its redesign in 2024. Members can earn and redeem Maharaja Points on Air India and Air India Express flights serving 104 destinations, as well as flights operated by 25 other Star Alliance member airlines.The programme has partnerships with over 100 brands across hospitality, retail, lifestyle and financial services, allowing members to earn points on travel and everyday spending.
Article Summary: Maharaja Club has added over five million members since its redesign in 2024. Members can earn and redeem Maharaja Points on Air India and Air India Express flights. The programme has partnerships with over 100 brands across hospitality, retail, lifestyle and financial services.

Article Title: Das flags priorities for banks to sustain growth
Article Text:
To achieve India's ambitious growth target of 8%, substantial investment is crucial for sectors like infrastructure, manufacturing, and small businesses.

Mumbai:

India’s 8% growth target is within reach, but sustaining that pace will require banks and financial institutions to finance infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and smaller businesses while expanding insurance and pension coverage, former RBI governor Shaktikanta Das said on Tuesday.He called for deeper credit and bond markets and a shift in household savings from physical assets to productive financial investments to support India’s ambition of becoming a developed economy by 2047.“In fact, in the recent months, I have stated on record that India is in a striking distance of 8% growth,” Das said in his keynote address at the Business Standard BFSI Summit 2026 here. He attributed the momentum to “the triple engines of macroeconomic stability; continuing structural reforms; and strategic policy initiatives to develop domestic capacity where we are largely import dependent”.Sustaining growth would be harder amid geopolitical conflicts, trade barriers, sanctions, unilateral tariffs and supply chain disruptions. Unlike earlier shocks, these disruptions had become prolonged, threatening energy and commodity markets, economic activity and financial stability. Das cautioned that consumption-related household borrowing required “careful and consistent monitoring”, signalling the need for continued scrutiny even as aggregate indicators improved.He identified stronger bank balance sheets as a key improvement, with lenders moving beyond high bad loans and weak capital adequacy to become well-capitalised and profitable.
Article Summary: India's 8% growth target is within reach, but sustaining that pace will require banks and financial institutions to finance infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and smaller businesses. Shaktikanta Das called for deeper credit and bond markets and a shift in household savings from physical assets to productive financial investments.

Article Title: Focus on covering more people, not just higher premiums: Irdai
Article Text:
Insurance companies must focus on covering more people and delivering effective protection for every rupee spent.

Mumbai:

Insurance companies must focus on covering more people and delivering effective protection for every rupee spent, rather than seeking higher premiums from existing policyholders, Irdai chairman Ajay Seth said.He also called for online insurance platforms to stick to their core role of helping customers compare products and buy policies, rather than expanding into physical distribution, using dynamic pricing or demanding contact details and do-not-disturb waiver before providing quotes.“We have to change our lens,” Seth said. “Instead of measuring insurance penetration and density, the industry should track lives and businesses covered, the effectiveness of protection and cover per rupee spent.” He was speaking during a fireside chat at a Business Standard BFSI event.Insurers serve the top 10-15% of the population reasonably well, but extending meaningful cover to the top 50% requires better affordability and quality. “Instead of chasing existing people for higher cover we should go for covering more people,” he said, adding that insurance must grow faster than the economy, not slower.Seth said digital insurance platforms should offer simplified products for easy price comparison and help customers find suitable cover at the lowest price.They should not dilute this role by building physical distribution networks, which operate on different dynamics. He also cautioned against the practice of offering dynamic pricing for covers by online platforms.“Dynamic pricing works in the airline industry, not in insurance,” he said, ruling out price changes on digital platforms. Customers should be able to compare prices without sharing personal details. Regulatory guardrails are needed to keep platforms focused on their core purpose.Health insurance is growing general insurance at 1.3 times the economy’s pace, but high customer dissatisfaction threatens to undermine growth. Seth called this an “uneasy, unstable equilibrium” and said insurers must disclose how much of the premiums they collect, they actually pay out in health insurance claims.Current settlement rates do not show this. “That information neither we track nor is it in the public domain,” he said. Seth was critical of the high churn in the health insurance portfolio under the guise of portability to show increased new business.Irdai is consulting insurers, intermediaries and policyholder representatives on distribution reforms to cut acquisition costs and ease premium pressure. Health insurance commissions average 24% across new policies and renewals; reducing them to 15-20% is the objective, he said. The regulator also wants to cut health insurance paperwork through the National Health Exchange. Cashless treatment accounts for around 60% of cases, rising by 1-2 percentage points a year, against a 90% longer-term target, he said.
Article Summary: Insurers serve the top 10-15% of the population reasonably well, but extending meaningful cover to the top 50% requires better affordability and quality. “Instead of chasing existing people for higher cover we should go for covering more people,” Irdai chairman Ajay Seth said.

Article Title: Maruti profit declines 27% despite record quarterly sales
Article Text:
Maruti Suzuki India

New Delhi: Record vehicle sales could not shield Maruti Suzuki from a sharp fall in quarterly profit as higher costs and investment losses squeezed earnings. India's largest carmaker reported standalone net profit of Rs 2,415 crore for July-Sept, down 27% year-on-year. Net sales rose 26% to a record Rs 50,616 crore, while vehicle sales increased 26.5% to an all-time quarterly high of over 6.9 lakh units.The earnings decline came as commodity inflation linked to West Asia disruptions pushed up costs. Total expenditure rose nearly 30% to Rs 50,604 crore, outpacing sales growth.Raw material and component expenditure increased 48% to Rs 37,488 crore amid higher production volumes and cost pressures. Operating profit fell 17% to Rs 2,804 crore from Rs 3,382 crore a year earlier.Mark-to-market losses on invested surplus added to the pressure, pulling non-operating income down to Rs 430 crore from Rs 966 crore.Demand remained strong, with small-car sales rising 35.9% and utility vehicle volumes growing 68.2%.Exports, however, declined to 1.08 lakh vehicles from 1.1 lakh vehicles in the corresponding quarter last year.Standalone revenue from operations, including servicing and ancillary income, increased to Rs 53,340 crore from Rs 42,332 crore. Consolidated net profit fell 26% to Rs 2,466 crore, while consolidated revenue reached Rs 53,356 crore. For April-Sept, standalone net profit declined 18% to Rs 5,767 crore from Rs 7,061 crore, reflecting sustained pressure on earnings despite the expansion in sales.
Article Summary: India's largest carmaker reported standalone net profit of Rs 2,415 crore for July-Sept. Net sales rose 26% to a record Rs 50,616 crore. Vehicle sales increased 26.5% to an all-time quarterly high of over 6.9 lakh units.

Article Title: Layoffs, rebranded: Corporate euphemisms meet the AI reset
Article Text: Bengaluru: Companies have never liked the word “fired”. It sounds too much like what actually happened. So every few years, corporate vocabulary comes to the rescue with a softer term for the same hard conversation.“Downsizing”, “rightsizing”, “restructuring”, “optimisation”, “organisational simplification” — corporate vocabulary keeps evolving. The person leaving may notice little difference, but the PowerPoint or press statement certainly sounds nicer.Now, AI is giving the corporate dictionary another reason to expand. Microsoft’s just come up with a new one – voluntary exit offer. Some 60,000 of its employees will be offered this VEO. To be fair, Microsoft is not saying it’s firing all of them. It’s only giving them the option to leave. But what would go through the minds of all those who do not accept it? Won’t they be working with a sense of the guillotine over their heads?Brand and business strategy specialist Harish Bijoor said the pressure on jobs remained, regardless of the terminology used. “Positions are being rejigged and layoffs are the norm of the day,” he said. Bijoor is less impressed by the linguistic makeover. “Corporate HR is notorious in its verbiage for such layoffs. Whatever you call it, a layoff is a layoff. Call what you want. A thorn is a thorn! That which we call by any other name is still a thorn. Apologies to William Shakespeare,” he said.Like fashion, corporate terminology moves in cycles. For as long as companies have been cutting jobs, they have been searching for gentler ways to describe it. The 1990s brought “rightsizing”, recasting downsizing as a correction in organisational size.The 2000s popularised “restructuring” and “reduction in force” (RIF), while the 2010s added “rebalancing”, “streamlining” and “resource action”. In 2023, it was the “year of efficiency”. Jobs disappear. The vocabulary survives, and occasionally gets a promotion.Jessie Paul, independent director and former CMO of Wipro , said AI is changing how companies think about workforce productivity and long-term staffing. “AI is causing a seismic shift in per capita revenue expectations from employees – Anthropic lists a whopping $6.6 million in revenue per employee. As all tech companies figure out how to get closer to this benchmark, they are engaging in long-term employee mix planning at a never-before scale. Companies want to make a distinction between longer-term personnel planning and distress-based terminations, so they’re coming up with new language. It will standardise soon,” she said.Indeed, the corporate world may find yet another gentler word for it. The person carrying the box out of the office probably won’t care.
Article Summary: Microsoft has just come up with a new one – voluntary exit offer. Some 60,000 of its employees will be offered this VEO. “Positions are being rejigged and layoffs are the norm of the day,” says Harish Bijoor.

School holiday October 29:

Will schools remain closed in Uttar Pradesh on October 29?

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: Anthropic files IPO, could be biggest ever
Article Text:
Anthropic is gearing up for its IPO, aiming to go public on the Nasdaq

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX IPO in June that raised a record $86 billion. An Anthropic IPO would also put the company ahead of OpenAI in going public in what is expected to be a pair of blockbuster stock debuts for the rival AI labs.The filing comes weeks after CEO Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as do its final valuation and offering price, but even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world’s most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela, by billions of dollars.The 335-page document showed Anthropic’s revenue is growing rapidly, but like many other tech companies going public, it has yet to turn a profit. The company behind the chatbot Claude reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. That compares to a loss of $13 billion in the same period a year earlier.Despite the losses, Anthropic, valued earlier this year at $965 billion by private investors, is reportedly set to see that value rise to $1.5 trillion or possibly $2 trillion, although its final valuation has not been established. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would rank among the world’s most valuable public companies, alongside Tesla.As for money raised, the offering could bring in as much as $100 billion, according to reports, surpassing the current record set by another one of Musk’s companies, SpaceX, earlier this year. Anthropic, meanwhile, emphasised the potential for its AI to “behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways” in the filing. If its technologies are not developed with adequate safeguards and oversight, it could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy. ”
Article Summary: Anthropic filed papers for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity. The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX IPO in June that raised a record $86 billion.

Article Title: Anthropic files for IPO: Losses, dividends & risks to humanity; what investors should know
Article Text:
Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion

Anthropic's 5 year journey

Here are five key takeaways.

Dividends: No payouts in sight

Voting rights: A founder-linked structure

Losses: An $80.7 billion half-year hit

Risks to humanity: The warning in the filing

What the founders get: A potentially historic payday

Anthropic’s planned stock market debut captures a central AI contradiction: surging demand and huge losses, alongside warnings that its technology could threaten humanity. The Claude maker plans to list on Nasdaq as ANT, but has yet to set the number of shares or their price range. The filing offers a closer look at what investors would be buying.Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. Revenue growth has been rapid, largely driven by business customers using Claude and related AI software. It expects losses to continue as it invests in computing, research, safety and expansion. Remaining competitive, it says, depends on advanced models, specialist staff and capital.The disclosures go beyond finances. They confirm there are no near-term dividends, describe a share structure that gives a founder-linked vehicle decisive voting power, and detail risks ranging from regulatory scrutiny to advanced AI moving beyond human control.Anthropic has never declared or paid cash dividends and does not expect to do so in the foreseeable future. It plans to retain available funds and future earnings for operations and expansion.Any dividend would be at the board’s discretion, based on its financial condition and capital needs. Its credit agreement also limits payouts, even if no money is outstanding under the facility.Anthropic has four authorised classes of common stock, with Class A and Class N as series of Participating Common Stock. Their voting rights differ. Class A shareholders get one vote per share on general matters. Class N generally carries no voting rights; Class T, issued to the LTBT, votes only on specified matters. Class E, intended for employees other than co-founders, also lacks general voting rights, subject to protections.Class F, to be issued to Founder LLC, carries votes equal to 50.1% of total voting power on general shareholder matters, including elections of directors other than Class T directors. Votes will be cast under the Founder LLC agreement, potentially limiting ordinary shareholders’ influence after listing.Anthropic’s net loss rose from $1.5 billion in 2023 to $8.3 billion in 2024 and $42 billion in 2025. In the six months to 30 June 2026, it lost $80.7 billion, compared with nearly $13 billion a year earlier.The figure needs context: $72.4 billion of the first-half loss came from changes in the fair value of convertible promissory notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, primarily as the value of outstanding notes rose alongside Anthropic’s valuation. The net loss is not a simple measure of cash spent on operations. Even so, the company says it is highly capital-intensive, expects costs and losses to continue, and may never achieve or sustain profitability.The filing says advanced AI systems could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” without safeguards, oversight and security. Misuse, replication, weaponisation or substantial autonomy could heighten those dangers. Even isolated or simulated harmful behaviour, it says, could trigger public concern, regulatory scrutiny, litigation and reputational damage, regardless of actual harm.Anthropic also describes “closing the loop”: using successive models to design, train, test and optimise the next generation. But flaws or biases could spread into later systems and become harder to detect or fix. AI research could outpace the ability to evaluate and safeguard new models, a concern alongside chief executive Dario Amodei’s calls for more cautious development. The company warns that the danger could grow as AI systems automate more of the research and development process itself.The offering could sharply increase the paper wealth of Anthropic’s seven founders, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister, co-founder Daniela. Reports say the founders collectively hold nearly 500 million shares, but their post-IPO ownership and any planned sales are unclear.The final valuation, offer price and size of the sale remain undecided, making any windfall uncertain. But Class F stock could preserve substantial founder-linked control as public investors buy in.
Article Summary: Claude maker plans to list on Nasdaq as ANT, but has yet to set the number of shares or their price range. Anthropic reported $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026 alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion. It expects losses to continue as it invests in computing, research and safety.

Article Title: Middle East conflict may end, but energy crisis will drag on: IEA chief explains
Article Text:
IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027

Oil prices near $120 a barrel add to economic pressure

Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies

Europe faces a difficult winter

With oil prices edging towards $120 a barrel and winter adding to concerns over fuel supplies, the global energy crisis could outlast the Iran war itself.International Energy Agency (IEA) executive director Fatih Birol has warned that energy markets are unlikely to return to their pre-war conditions in 2027, urging governments and businesses to put energy security first.Speaking at the Singapore International Energy Week conference on Monday, Birol said that the conflict, which began in late February, had upended expectations of a surplus in the energy market this year. Instead, disruptions to global energy flows have tightened supplies and pushed up oil benchmarks and refined fuel prices."I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started," Birol said.He called on countries and companies to prepare for a prolonged period of uncertainty, with energy security taking priority while they also consider what comes next."So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today," he said.The pressure on oil markets has already been visible in prices.More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sent Brent crude futures soaring to $117 a barrel on Friday, their highest level in nearly six months. Prices eased to $115 per barrel on Monday but still remained about 59% above their pre-war level."Oil prices are flirting with $120 a barrel and the prices for products are even much higher," Birol said.While he declined to predict where oil prices would go next, he warned that costs at these levels were becoming a major burden for several economies."I can tell you that the current price of oil is, for some countries, for example in Europe, maybe not so high and affordable. But in many parts of the world, having almost $120 oil prices is having a major impact on trade deficits."Oil is not the only concern. As winter approaches, Birol is also worried about the availability and cost of refined products, particularly diesel, which is used for heating in parts of the West.Demand for diesel typically rises during the colder months, just as several refineries are scheduled to undergo maintenance, adding another pressure point for fuel markets."I am worried on top of that for refined products because we are entering...winter season. Some parts of the world, where typically diesel demand goes high and several refineries are going through maintenance period."Europe, meanwhile, faces a difficult winter on the gas front. Countries have decided to cut imports of Russian gas, while the Iran war has added to the strain by disrupting gas exports from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates."In Europe, we are facing a tough winter because European countries have decided to cut gas imports from Russia and with the additional problem now rising from the Iran war, namely Qatar and the Emirates not being able to export gas as they were before, will put significant pressure on gas markets."The energy crisis could also give nuclear power a fresh push. Birol expects a "strong comeback" for the sector as countries grapple with the current situation. The IEA's recent survey found that 90 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity was under construction, the highest level in the past four decades, he said.
Article Summary: IEA executive director Fatih Birol warns energy markets are unlikely to return to pre-war conditions in 2027. He urges governments and businesses to put energy security first. Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies in Europe and the U.S.

Article Title: Crude prices fall from six-month highs; WTI stands at $101 per barrel, Brent costs $115
Article Text:
Crude prcies fall from six month-highs, but trade beyond $100 per barrel

Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern

Supply measures fail to reverse the rally

Oil prices fell over 1% on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week. Despite the decline, prices remained elevated, with Brent crude hovering near $115 per barrel as continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns over global oil supplies alive.The US Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision is another factor investors will watch as crude enters a potentially volatile week.WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41%, or $1.65, to $115.1 per barrel.The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies. Brent recorded a 6% gain for the week, while WTI advanced 2.3%, taking prices close to six-month highs.The security situation remained tense over the weekend. The Houthis said they had attacked a Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday, while Saudi Arabia reported intercepting additional missiles and drones on Sunday. The country's main airport resumed partial operations the same day, following damage from an earlier round of Houthi attacks. The militant group has vowed to continue targeting the facility.Developments around the Strait of Hormuz and the security of energy infrastructure are expected to influence crude prices in the coming days. Brent has already crossed $117 per barrel, and analysts said any disruption to energy facilities or shipping through the strait could push global prices towards $120 per barrel. A credible move towards de-escalation, however, could lead to a sharp correction."The near-term bias remains bullish but highly headline-driven; traders should avoid chasing sharp rallies and monitor geopolitical developments, Fed guidance and weekly inventory data for directional confirmation," said Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking.The latest price rally has been driven by escalating US-Iran tensions, fears of renewed military action, attacks on Saudi infrastructure and threats to important shipping routes, Mishra said. These developments have sustained the geopolitical risk premium in oil prices.Navneet Damani, head of research - commodities at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said, "The rally gathered pace as attention returned to escalating attacks around the Hormuz and Saudi Arabia, reviving concerns over energy infrastructure and export security."Further uncertainty has emerged from reports that the US and Israel had prepared plans to target Iranian energy infrastructure, including nuclear facilities near Natanz, after the US mid-term elections on November 3. Iran warned of repercussions if Washington and Tel Aviv launched an attack, adding to concerns in the market.Efforts to ease supply concerns have so far done little to bring prices down. The International Energy Agency has indicated its readiness to release more strategic stocks, while the G7's additional 100 million barrels largely involves accelerating an existing release programme. The first Russian diesel cargo bound for the US has also failed to reverse the upward trend.According to Damani, market participants are now looking for evidence that these measures will translate into meaningful additional supplies, rather than responding to announcements alone."Although crude flows through Hormuz have shown some recovery, elevated freight costs, constrained regional shipments and persistent security threats continue to undermine export reliability. With physical supply yet to normalise, the risk premium remains elevated, and the balance of risks continues to favour the upside, though credible progress towards de-escalation could still trigger sharp profit-taking," Damani added.The market will also track weekly US inventory estimates from the American Petroleum Institute and the US Energy Information Administration, alongside Cushing crude inventories. These figures could offer further direction as traders assess the state of supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41% to $115.1 per barrel. The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies.

Article Title: France’s economic woes: Debt nears 122% of GDP, growth forecast at just 0.4%
Article Text:
France’s debt, taxes and borrowing costs rise as economic growth slows

France’s public debt nears 122% of GDP

Government spending accounts for 57.2% of GDP

France faces higher borrowing costs

France’s growth forecast falls to 0.4%

France is facing mounting pressure on two fronts: growing public anger over the cost of living and an economy struggling with high debt, taxes and weak growth. Student protests that began with school blockades have spread, turning violent, putting the spotlight on the country’s economic troubles and deepening political tensions.The rising cost of living is one of the concerns behind the demonstrations, which began largely peacefully but disrupted schools before escalating into wider unrest and pockets of violence involving young people on Saturday. The issue is not unique to France, but it comes at a difficult time for the country’s economy.France is also struggling to bring its public finances under control. Carsten Brzeski, global chief of macro at ING bank, said “France is not Greece”, referring to the financial crisis that shook the European Union in 2009. However, France has repeatedly failed to meet its targets for spending, economic growth and cost-cutting.With President Emmanuel Macron nearing the end of his nearly decade-long tenure, the state of the country’s finances is also expected to be a key issue in the race to succeed him next spring.France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP).The government has warned that the figure could rise further. Three weeks ago, it said the budget would again exceed European Union spending limits, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP, setting a new record, AP reported.The growing debt leaves the government with difficult choices. It needs to reduce spending or raise taxes, which are already among the highest in Europe.Gilbert Cette, an economics professor at Neoma Business School in Paris, described the debt as “enormous”, saying, “France’s entire economic policy is constrained by such a sizable debt level.”Cette said France had shown “talent” in both increasing government spending and cutting taxes in recent years, making it harder to get public finances back on track.Brzeski also warned that France’s approach to economic reforms was affecting its credibility. Writing last week, he said, “Greece’s credibility was destroyed by false statistics; France’s is being eroded by false promises and the inability or unwillingness to start fiscal and structural reforms,”High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country’s economic output, according to Eurostat, the European Union’s statistics agency. The EU average was just under 50%.A large share of this spending goes towards healthcare, pensions and subsidies for businesses. With government expenditure already making up such a large part of the economy, reducing it further would require difficult decisions.France also has one of the highest tax burdens in the European Union. Tax revenue and social contributions accounted for 45.2% of GDP in 2024, putting the country a close second behind Denmark, according to Eurostat. The EU average was just over 40%.This leaves the government with limited room to raise taxes further to reduce the deficit. Cutting spending is another option, but it would mean making choices about areas that already account for a significant share of the economy.The cost of borrowing is adding to the pressure on France’s public finances. The yield on its 10-year government bond stood at 4.96% as of Tuesday.Higher bond yields mean the government has to pay more to borrow money. This can leave less room in the budget for other priorities, including pensions, education, healthcare, defence and social programmes.Germany, the European Union’s largest economy, faces lower borrowing costs. Its equivalent 10-year government bond, known as the Bund, had a yield of about 3.4%.The gap between French and German 10-year bond yields has widened, highlighting the difference in borrowing costs between the two countries. This adds to the challenges facing France as it tries to manage its debt and spending.France’s economic outlook remains weak. The International Monetary Fund has forecast growth of just 0.4% for the country this year, the lowest rate among developed economies.The forecast is well below the expected growth rates for both the global economy and advanced economies. Global output is projected to grow by 3.1% this year, while advanced economies are expected to expand by 2.1%.France’s projected growth is around one-third of Germany’s forecast rate and half of Italy’s. Japan, which has the second-lowest growth forecast among developed countries, is expected to grow by 0.7%.Slow growth makes it harder for France to manage its public finances while dealing with high debt, substantial government spending and an already heavy tax burden. Rising borrowing costs further add to the pressure.With the economy growing slowly and public finances under strain, France faces difficult choices over how to control its debt and spending. These economic challenges are unfolding alongside political divisions and protests over the cost of living, while the state of public finances is set to remain an important issue ahead of next spring’s presidential succession race.
Article Summary: France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP) The government has warned that the figure could rise further, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP. High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country's economic output, according to Eurostat.

Article Title: US Fed expected to hold rates as inflation, energy costs weigh ahead of midterms
Article Text:
US Fed expected to hold interest rates steady despite persistent inflation (representative image)

Inflation pressures complicate Fed's rate decision

Former Fed official says economic data favour further hikes

Trump's criticism of Fed independence

The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week, despite persistent inflation and market expectations of at least one more rate hike before the end of the year, according to analysts cited by news agency AFP.The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet over two days, with its interest rate decision scheduled for 2 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Wednesday.At its September meeting, the Fed raised its benchmark federal funds rate for the first time in three years, taking the target range to 3.75%-4%. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%, which it has missed for more than five years.The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party.The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, reached a pandemic-era peak of 7.2% in 2022 before a series of interest rate increases brought it down to around 2.2% by late 2024.However, inflation subsequently rose again amid Trump's economic policies, including tariffs that disrupted global trade and the US war with Iran. The PCE index reached a three-year high of 3.9% in May.Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, global energy prices have surged, with retaliatory actions by Tehran sharply restricting oil and gas supplies through the Gulf. Higher energy costs have also begun feeding into the prices of other goods and services, putting affordability at the forefront of concerns ahead of the midterm elections.The Fed faces the challenge of controlling inflation while supporting the labour market. Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs, potentially slowing economic activity and curbing price pressures, but they can also weigh on employment.The US economy has also been dealing with weakening consumer confidence and signs of stress in an otherwise resilient jobs market. The latest consumer confidence survey from the Conference Board was expected to show a further decline in October after confidence fell in September to its lowest level in more than a decade.Loretta Mester, a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, told AFP that the timing of the meeting ahead of the elections would not influence policymakers' decision."The Fed doesn't take into account any kind of political issues in that FOMC room," she said. "It really is based on the economics."Mester argued that economic conditions supported further monetary tightening, pointing to a stable labour market and inflation remaining above the central bank's target."The data that's come in continue to show a stable labor market and continue to show inflation above target," she said, adding that there was no evidence of inflation moving towards the target."The economics would suggest then you need to continue raising rates."However, Mester said most policymakers appeared reluctant to move too quickly. She expected the Fed could hold rates steady in October and consider another increase at its next meeting in early December.Wendy Edelberg, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, also said that central bankers would prefer to avoid becoming part of the political debate ahead of the elections."It's unhelpful for everyone if the Fed gets wrapped up in all the political discourse right before an election," she said.Edelberg added that raising rates in December rather than October would have limited economic implications.She viewed a possible delay less as a concession to Trump, who has repeatedly called for lower interest rates, and more as a way for the Fed to avoid becoming a target of political criticism.Trump has repeatedly criticised the Federal Reserve over interest rates, which he considers too high. However, he has so far refrained from directing similar criticism at Kevin Warsh, whom he appointed to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed chair.Since returning to power last year, Trump has mounted an unprecedented challenge to the central bank's independence. His administration launched a criminal investigation into Powell and attempted to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook.The investigation into Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh's confirmation by the Senate, while the legal battle over Cook's removal continued despite a Supreme Court decision nullifying an earlier attempt to dismiss her.Last week, Cook declined to attend a hearing in a White House investigation into mortgage fraud allegations, which she denies.Meanwhile, the Fed's rate decision will come during a busy week for US economic data.Investors and policymakers were also awaiting updates on inflation, consumer confidence and third-quarter economic growth, alongside earnings reports from major companies.
Article Summary: US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%. The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress.

Article Title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
Article Text:
File photo: A shopper looks at the section of a grocery store in Fort Worth, Texas (Picture credit: AP)

Independent voters report weaker sentiment

Inflation expectations remain elevated

Federal Reserve decision due next week

US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on households' views of the economy, a University of Michigan survey showed on Friday, with affordability emerging as a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The university's Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.Economists polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 46.3, which was also the preliminary estimate for October.October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began."Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."The survey's findings coincided with political polling showing that voters held a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's handling of it, Reuters reported.Millions of Americans have already cast early ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.Polls indicated Republicans were likely to lose control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate also potentially at stake. Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll stood at a record low, amid a surge in fuel prices following his decision to attack Iran in late February.The University of Michigan survey found that the decline in sentiment was driven by respondents who identified as independents, a group that includes swing voters.Their sentiment score fell to 42.4 in October from 47.7 in September, putting it just above May's record low of 40.6. Sentiment scores among Democrats and Republicans improved.The survey also found that more independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents reporting inflation pressures as a financial burden had risen by 27%, while the figure among Republicans had increased by 52%. Among Democrats, the increase was 15%.Households with little or no exposure to the stock market had also increasingly cited high prices as a financial burden compared with the beginning of the year. The stock market had recently climbed rapidly amid enthusiasm for investments in artificial intelligence.The survey's measure of consumers' expectations for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 4.7% in October from 4.6% in September. The measure had stood at 3.4% in February, before the US-Israeli war with Iran began.Expectations for inflation over the next five years increased to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, shortly after the conflict began.In an accompanying report, Hsu said persistently elevated inflation expectations in the period following the Covid-19 pandemic posed a risk to the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target. The target had remained unmet for more than five years, she wrote."Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu said.She also cautioned that relatively resilient consumer spending, despite negative views of the economy, required close attention. If households were spending now to avoid expected price increases in the future, bringing inflation down could become more difficult, she added.Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to meet in Washington next week. Despite recent inflation readings that came in higher than expected, they were broadly expected to keep the policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.The Fed had raised the rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September. Most officials had indicated a need for higher interest rates, while key policymakers had also expressed willingness to wait for more data before making their next move.
Article Summary: Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began. More independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances.

Article Title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms, offering relief to Maine
Article Text:
The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Collins seeks relief for Maine businesses

Trade tensions strain US-Canada ties

US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine, a state whose economy has been affected by the trade dispute with Canada.The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30.Collins said she had "secured" the exemptions for products important to Maine's agricultural sector, including blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democratic candidate, said farmers in her state depend on supplies from Canada that are difficult or expensive to source elsewhere.She said many farmers "rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."The senator's intervention comes as Democrats target her seat in their bid to take control of Congress from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.Maine shares a border with Canada, and businesses in the state have felt the effects of Trump's trade policies.The partial tariff relief could ease costs for some businesses, although the introduction of duties on other Canadian products means the changes will not benefit every sector.Also Read: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean The United States and Canada have closely connected economies, with roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports going to the US. Trade relations have deteriorated since negotiations between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a fresh round of tariffs.Earlier US duties on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium and lumber have hurt businesses, contributed to job losses and weighed on economic growth. Canada entered a technical recession this year after its economy contracted for two consecutive quarters.The tariffs imposed after the collapse of trade talks affected goods worth around $20 billion, equivalent to 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US. The targeted products ranged from hockey sticks to cement.Since returning to office for his second term, Trump has imposed extensive tariffs on imports from both allies and rivals, arguing that other countries have taken advantage of the United States.His administration has also linked some threatened tariffs to broader political and foreign policy goals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports. The move comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine. The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Article Title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
Article Text:
Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert.

India ranked ninth globally among services displaying PHP information.

BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services.
